title: A mechanism's recurrence across retained kernels measures how often a rationale was copied, not whether it helped: four corpora disagree with the comments on the streaming store, and StoreParameters should not grow a reuse field

evidence.note: No open-cake-ir campaign and no device. Three external corpora plus this project's own source are read; every number below is theirs, measured on their hardware under their harness.

Five distinct tasks (002, 003, 022, 025, 026) emit st.global.cs for the output store, each with the same stated reason: the output is write-once and should not displace the weight that is reused across rows. Read as five independent confirmations this looks decisive. It is one rationale carried across five files.

Measured, directive=avoid: 'Store policy sweep (cs/wt/plain) showed identical performance -- the output store policy is not a differentiator at this BW ceiling. st.global.cs was kept for L2 hygiene but does not change measured latency.' A sibling lesson records st.global.cs.v4 regressing against plain uint4 stores, and a third records __ldcs+__ldca on the inputs regressing to 0.8113x from 1.154x.

Independent of the bank, on B300 sm_103a: clean_start/norm, 167 candidates over 3 tasks and 11 workflows, st_cs present in 123 with median 7.929x against 44 without at 8.660x, delta -0.731. The same table puts cuda_graph at +4.948 and shared-memory use at +4.382 in that family, so the store policy is not merely small, it is beside the two effects that dominate.

StoreParameters carries only `coalesced`, while LoadParameters carries LoadReuse{REUSED,STREAMED} which backends/triton.py:1184 lowers to evict_last or cache_modifier='.cg'. The asymmetry is real. What is not established is that closing it would buy anything.

observation: Counting how many retained kernels contain a mechanism counts copies of a belief, not observations of an effect. The streaming store is the clean instance: it survives in five baselines because it is cheap and sounds right, and three independent measurements -- a 4090 sweep, a B200 eviction-policy probe, and 167 B300 candidates -- say it is neutral at best and slightly negative at worst. A fourth corpus fact sharpens it: the same B200 lesson records evict_first as a win on the pointer-arithmetic path and a regression on the TMA block_ptr path, so even on the load side the sign of a reuse hint is conditioned on the route, not on the operand. open-cake-ir is not currently exposed to that: backends/triton.py:449 refuses any load whose movement is not LoadMovement.GLOBAL, which is the path where the hint measured positive. It becomes a live question the moment the Triton route admits TMA.
proposed_change: Do not add a reuse or cache-policy field to StoreParameters; the asymmetry with LoadParameters is not by itself a reason, and no measurement supports closing it. Record the rationale as refuted rather than deleting it, because it says where a plausible causal model is wrong. Separately, when the Triton route admits LoadMovement.TMA, make the LoadReuse lowering route-conditioned rather than unconditional, and cite this record for why; until then pin the TRITON_LOAD_MOVEMENT refusal with a test so the constraint surfaces at the moment it stops being latent.
